docs.title: QGIS pypopRF
docs.text:
pypopRF creates gridded population maps from census-zone totals and aligned numeric raster covariates. The plugin was developed by the WorldPop SDI Team and contains its own modified numerical core, related to the upstream pypopRF work. The local implementation and configuration described here are the contract for this plugin build.

The interface manages projects, inputs, an isolated analysis engine and run history. Computation runs in a separate 64-bit Python 3.12 environment rather than importing the numerical stack into QGIS. Existing projects and earlier run results are preserved.

docs.title: Modernized workflow
docs.text:
These guides describe version 0.3.7 in this repository, not an older released plugin. They are shipped with the ZIP; an already deployed website may be behind this checkout until a separate documentation deployment occurs.

Home → Engine → Project → Input data → Settings → Run analysis → Results

Home provides the next step and project identity. Engine discovers compatible Python and prepares the isolated environment. Project distinguishes a selected folder from a successfully opened project. Inputs and settings remain gated until activation. The checklist, task status and Run/Stop action stay below every tab; Details retains diagnostics. All plugin windows use one independent light scheme.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
• Installation: prepare the plugin and engine.
  • Quick start: create or open a project and run it.
  • Projects: selected folder, activation, storage and backups.
  • Interface: Home, Engine, Project, Input data, Settings, Results and Details.
  • Input data: grid, census, covariates and optional masks/groups.
  • Settings: controls, target units and spatial validation.
  • Running analysis: inspect completed outputs.
  • Troubleshooting: recover without deleting original data.
  • Development: architecture, checks and reproducible packaging.

docs.title: Calculation
docs.text:
When inputs need alignment, use the guided Prepare / align inputs… workflow to create a separate derived project, not overwrite the originals. When a run finishes, Results combines a saved-evidence quality dashboard, QGIS layer actions and explicit cell-centre population summaries. These conveniences do not relax the data or scientific contracts below.

  1. Validate the complete raster alignment and population-table contracts.
  2. Apply optional water exclusion to a temporary zone grid.
  3. Extract covariate means and count eligible pixels independently of covariate order.
  4. Fit and validate a seeded Random Forest using the selected target transform.
  5. Predict density weights where the selected predictors are valid.
  6. Allocate each census zone's total across eligible positive weights.
  7. Read back population maps and verify the total of each zone before completion.

Optional population support produces a separate constrained map. Optional age/sex tables produce group maps joined by zone ID, with each group's totals checked separately. Missing support for positive population causes an explicit failure rather than an apparently successful partial population map.

docs.title: What the results establish
docs.text:
Population outputs conserve the supplied totals within numerical tolerance. That verifies allocation arithmetic, not fine-scale geographic accuracy. A map can conserve every total while locating people incorrectly within zones. Training on zonal means and applying the fitted model to pixels also involves a change of spatial scale which requires independent validation.

The default model validation holds out centroid-based spatial blocks and refits the full modelling procedure within each training fold. It records block geometry and limitations, including the absence of separation buffers. Scores refer to held-out zone-average density. Independent finer-resolution population data are needed before making claims about pixel accuracy.

Each completed run records input-resource hashes, source-code hashes, effective configuration, CV provenance and output-artifact metadata in its manifest and associated files. The interface only presents verified complete runs as results.

docs.title: Project and attribution
docs.text:
Project development and issues are hosted at wpgp/QGIS-pypopRF. Use GitHub Issues for reproducible reports, including diagnostics and the plugin/QGIS/engine versions.

Please preserve the authorship information in the repository's CITATION.cff and use it when citing the software. See the repository LICENSE and individual file notices for licensing information. The project's documented origins and WorldPop SDI attribution remain unchanged by this modernization.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: The plugin has two deliberately separate execution environments: the QGIS/Qt adapter and a locked CPython 3.12 numerical engine. Keep scientific imports and calculation inside the engine. Plugin activation must not run pip, add binary packages to the QGIS path, or select another interpreter implicitly for host installation.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
__init__.py, metadata.txt, qgis_pypoprf.py  QGIS plugin entrypoint
core/pypoprf/                            isolated numerical engine
  algorithms/                           extraction, RF and allocation
  config/, utils/                       engine validation and raster tasks
gui/
  dialogs/, forms/, widgets/             native Qt views and Designer form
  icons/                                packaged vector control/action indicators
  presenters/                           project, results and preparation views
controllers/                            owned asynchronous workflows
services/                               configuration, runtime and saved metadata
shared/                                 stdlib atomic/environment contracts
tests/
  engine/, services/, gui/               focused regression suites
  integration/, native/, packaging/     workflow, real QGIS and ZIP checks
scripts/                                build, test, translation and upload tools
docs/                                   maintained user/developer guides
.local/                                 ignored reports, experiments and legacy files
dist/                                   ignored generated plugin ZIPs

The required QGIS files remain at the plugin root. Internal modules are not compatibility aliases: update their imports when developing against this layout. The public engine commands remain python -m core.pypoprf and python -m core.pypoprf.tools.

Boundary Rule core Numerical/geospatial computation; no Qt, GUI, controllers or provisioning services. gui Widgets, dialog composition, native layer presentation and desktop actions; no numerical imports. controllers Owned tasks and view coordination; no numerical imports. services Config files, runtime setup/process ownership and saved artifacts; no Qt or numerical imports. shared Standard library only; no engine, services or GUI dependencies.

The main dialog composes project/input, result and preparation presenters rather than mixing all tab behavior into one class. Dialogs and reusable widgets live separately. Opening folders is a GUI desktop action, not a file-copy service. Runtime provisioning uses the shared environment contract; importing that contract does not start setup, mutate the parent environment or import numerical libraries. services/owned_process.py implements platform process ownership; services/process_exit_guard.py verifies actual Windows launch descendants.

docs.title: GUI state and appearance contracts
docs.text:
ProjectInputsPresenter.selection_is_active() distinguishes folder selection from successful activation. Central readiness refresh also calls refresh_project_action(): an active folder shows Project open (disabled), a different candidate requires explicit Create/Open, and a failed candidate is never labelled active. Duplicate direct activation calls do not reload settings or reinitialize logging. Worker completion must restore this state, not blindly enable the activation button. Keep location/configured-path/log checks before activating any new folder.

gui/widgets/light_theme.py owns one full light palette, window-scoped QSS and parent-owned event guard. Never call application-global palette/style/font setters to implement plugin colors. Vector glyphs in gui/icons/ must remain in the packaging allowlist; Run/Stop have explicit normal and disabled variants. FittedLabel bounds rendered footer lines without losing caller-bounded text; tests must check actual font/DPI geometry, not just source newline count.

Maintain native state, import, lifecycle, hostile-host-theme and project-activation tests alongside changes. Public screenshots use real QGIS synthetic fixtures; private user paths/data and qualification reports stay in .local/.

QProcess stdout carries newline-delimited JSON progress/result events; stderr carries diagnostics. A successful result requires normal exit, a matching complete result event, a complete manifest and present contained result paths. Progress alone never establishes successful completion. Native process/thread completion determines when a controller can release its owned resources.

Before analysis or preparation starts, services/engine_snapshot.py freezes a bounded, verified copy of engine/shared code, provenance resources and dependency locks in the owned job cache. The child starts with -I -B, verifies the snapshot manifest, exact file inventory and installed dependency versions before importing the numerical engine, and uses an external job working directory. Replacing the installed plugin cannot change that child's imports or recorded source hashes. Analysis manifests distinguish verified_snapshot from direct CLI live_source execution and retain the frozen-manifest digest. No snapshot is shared between jobs or removed before the actual owned child exits.

Setup creates a venv at its permanent unique location. It does not move a venv after creation. Installation accepts exact pinned requirements, uses binary wheels, checks package consistency and native imports, and activates through a small atomic pointer after health checks. A failed update preserves the previous environment. Readiness and discovery belong in background workers as they run subprocesses. Cancellation must reach those subprocess checks as well as setup.

docs.title: Engine development environment
docs.text:
Use an independent environment, not the QGIS interpreter:

py -3.12 -m venv .venv-dev
.\.venv-dev\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
.\.venv-dev\Scripts\python -m pytest -m "not qgis" -q
.\.venv-dev\Scripts\python -m ruff check core gui controllers services shared qgis_pypoprf.py __init__.py scripts tests

On Linux use an installed python3.12, then .venv-dev/bin/python for the same commands. requirements-dev.txt includes the exact engine lock plus test and lint tools. Dependency upgrades are a separate change: validate clean installation and regression/artifact compatibility before replacing the lock.

For native development, build the plugin ZIP and install it into a dedicated QGIS profile using its plugin manager. This avoids suggesting a hard-coded profile directory or a module directory name containing a hyphen.

docs.title: Tests and acceptance
docs.text:
The headless suite tests production code with temporary GeoTIFF/CSV fixtures, including keyed joins, NoData, alignment, singleton zones, population conservation, target inversion, CV isolation, model reload, cancellation, atomic failures and provenance. The bundled Rwanda test checks extraction and 416-zone allocation; it skips explicitly if the case-study data are absent.

Qt doubles exercise controller state and error paths; they do not validate native Qt ownership or widget binding compatibility. Run tests/native/ in a genuine QGIS application/runtime with an available separate engine. Offscreen container acceptance is useful, but it does not replace an interactive operating-system smoke test. CI configuration in .github/workflows/test.yml declares the actual current test matrix.

The Windows headless job also creates an empty temporary engine cache and invokes the real locked setup and health checks. Installing development dependencies or using a prepared engine is not evidence that a fresh Windows installation works. New environments use a shorter full-UUID basename; legacy verified names remain accepted without moving their virtual environments. Arbitrarily long custom cache paths remain subject to operating-system and wheel path limits.

scripts/run_native_tests.py discovers all test modules in tests/native/ by default; this includes the original adapter, preparation/layer/AOI workflow and quality widget tests plus isolated actual-installer replacement/recovery tests. Set PYPOPRF_TEST_PLUGIN_ROOT to the freshly extracted plugin and PYPOPRF_TEST_PLUGIN_ZIP to the same verified ZIP. On Windows, PYPOPRF_TEST_ENGINE must name a standalone prepared engine, not the portable QGIS host interpreter. The installer subprocess tests redirect home, cache, profile and Qt INI settings into a nonce-owned temporary directory before any settings write; they never use an existing desktop profile. They include a Windows-only copied-DLL, normal-process-exit migration fixture, not forced DLL unloading or manual deletion of a user installation.

Windows launcher termination is not itself proof that the redirected Python child has exited: the adapter asynchronously checks held, birth-identified Windows process handles before releasing metadata or deleting owned scratch. Tracking failures remain explicit and do not falsely establish cleanup safety.

Maintainer ZIP verification checks portable raw member names (including Windows aliases/device names), regular-file inventory and manifest/version consistency without extracting files. It rejects more than 10,000 members, a member larger than 25 MiB, more than 100 MiB expanded data, a manifest larger than 4 MiB, or an archive larger than 25 MB before content verification. These are resource and consistency checks, not publisher signatures or proof of authentic code.

An access-denied candidate can be excluded only when a limited query proves its creation time lies outside every held parent's lifetime. Query-only handles are never retained or used to establish exit; Windows live-process exit-time fields are undefined. Fully inaccessible or possibly owned children remain fail-closed, with explicit tracking diagnostics rather than premature resource cleanup.

The extra tools protocol is python -m core.pypoprf.tools --request absolute-request.json --cancel-file marker. Schema1 requests choose inspect, prepare or population_summary; both progress and final events carry an ownership nonce. Complete output requires an owned new directory, fixed report.json, matching request ID and (for preparation) validated config.yaml. GUI preparation additionally carries the inspected expected_inputs fingerprint list. AOI summaries can bind a population map to its recorded artifact SHA, and explain partial coverage separately. No tool imports QGIS into the engine or numerical libraries into the QGIS host.

The research command compares predeclared candidates on identical spatial outer folds and saves the predictions, source hashes and split provenance:

python -m scripts.benchmark_models --output .local/benchmarks/new_comparison --trees 100 --spatial-grid 4 4

It requires a fresh output directory and does not change the production model. Experiment results and qualification evidence belong under ignored .local/, not in Git or the runtime ZIP. Do not turn an improvement on one block partition into a pixel-accuracy guarantee. Old generated resources and historical screenshots are archived locally; the live interface uses filesystem icons and the maintained Designer form, not a PyQt5-only generated resources module.

tests/packaging/test_architecture.py checks import boundaries, canonical and plugin-alias loading, and an extracted ZIP without repository paths. Tests, maintained documentation, dependency locks, scripts and CI are project sources; private audits/reviews, run outputs, caches, environments and experiments are not. Commit a coherent tested stage with explicit paths; never force-add .local/ or dist/, and do not push without the owner's request.

docs.title: Numerical and lifecycle invariants
docs.text:
• Inputs are never rewritten by validation or replaced by output publication.
  • Census joins are by unique ID; density support comes from eligible mastergrid pixels.
  • Missing predictors remain distinct from numeric zero; errors propagate from every tile.
  • A positive population without positive eligible prediction support fails explicitly.
  • Every published population raster is read back and checked per zone.
  • Every outer validation fit recomputes preprocessing and selection from training data only.
  • Spatial grouping metadata states CRS, scale, centroid method and lack of buffers.
  • Failed/cancelled attempts cannot become complete maps or remove earlier runs.
  • Temporary files and process/thread resources belong to one run and are cleaned only after use ends.

Model bundles include feature order, target transform, version and training-grid contracts. Treat joblib as trusted executable serialization; mismatched old model/scaler pairs require retraining. Effective settings must be recorded using Settings.to_config() rather than copying only explicit YAML fields.

docs.title: Packaging and contribution
docs.text:
python scripts/build_plugin.py --output dist/pypopRF.zip

The builder uses an explicit runtime allowlist, deterministic ZIP metadata and a hashed package manifest. User data, tests, benchmark outputs and local engine environments do not belong in the distributable. python -m scripts.plugin_upload is an explicit maintainer publishing command; normal builds and activation do not upload anything.

docs.title: Release checklist
docs.text:
1. Finish regression/native-QGIS checks and owner acceptance before formatting a release. Keep private qualification evidence under ignored .local/.
  2. Update the canonical version in metadata.txt (also read by the engine). For a stable release set experimental=False and put the matching version/date first in CHANGELOG.md. Retain repository and file-specific license/authorship notices.
  3. Run python scripts/check_release.py, headless tests, Ruff and native tests against the exact newly built ZIP. Build twice and compare SHA-256 hashes; preserve the previously accepted archive before replacing local artifacts.
  4. Build the documentation with mkdocs build --strict and check local links and packaged assets. Commit only maintained project sources, tests, guides and CI.
  5. With owner approval, push the commit and require GitHub Actions to pass for that commit. Local checks do not establish remote CI success. Pushing master also triggers the existing documentation deployment workflow.
  6. Prepare a v<version> tag pointing at the accepted commit. Tag pushes run the test workflow and verify tag/metadata identity. Publishing to GitHub or QGIS remains a separate, explicitly authorized maintainer action.

For example, python scripts/build_plugin.py --output dist/pypopRF-0.3.7.zip builds this version without tagging, uploading or deploying it. The CI test workflow has read-only repository permissions; it does not publish packages.

When submitting a change, include the concrete before/after behaviour, meaningful validation and material limits. Preserve unrelated user changes and historical data. Keep source attribution, CITATION.cff, the repository LICENSE and individual file notices intact. Report reproducible issues through GitHub Issues.

docs.title: Installation and updates
docs.text: These instructions describe version 0.3.7. Use a matching plugin ZIP or build one from this checkout; older packages do not contain this workflow. A local ZIP build is not publication to GitHub or the QGIS plugin repository.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
You need Why QGIS in the declared 3.44–4.x range Hosts the interface and QGIS layers; local native acceptance targets 3.44 and 4.2. A valid ZIP built from this checkout Earlier released packages do not contain this UI/runtime workflow. Separately installed 64-bit CPython 3.12 Runs the isolated calculation engine; QGIS's Python may differ. Network and writable user cache for initial setup Downloads and verifies the locked binary wheels. An analysis folder outside the installed plugin/cache Keeps input data and completed runs independent of updates.

Obtain QGIS from its official download page. OSGeo4W is not a plugin requirement: the plugin does not depend on one particular Windows installation method. It requires working QGIS/PyQt bindings for the interface and a separate compatible calculation Python. Do not select QGIS's embedded interpreter merely because it is installed on the same PC.

docs.title: Two separate components
docs.text:
The interface runs inside QGIS. Numerical processing runs in a dedicated, per-user 64-bit CPython 3.12 virtual environment. Enabling the plugin never runs pip, modifies QGIS Python, or imports the numerical libraries.

The declared range is QGIS 3.44–4.x. Native acceptance targets Windows AMD64 and Linux glibc x86_64 QGIS 3.44 / Qt 5 and QGIS 4.2 / Qt 6, each with a separate engine. macOS, ARM and musl are not qualified by this build. The development guide explains the reproducible checks; private local qualification reports are not published as repository files.

docs.title: Install the plugin ZIP
docs.text:
1. Use a verified plugin ZIP matching this version, or, if working from source, build with python scripts/build_plugin.py from the repository root. Building the interface archive itself needs Python's standard library, not pip or QGIS. The resulting ZIP excludes datasets, tests and developer environments.
  2. In QGIS, choose Plugins → Manage and Install Plugins → Install from ZIP and select the generated ZIP.
  3. Enable pypopRF and open its dialog.
  4. On Home, follow the next-step controls. On Engine, choose a recommended compatible Python from the discovered list, then choose Set up engine. If none is found, Get Python 3.12… explains the requirement and can open the official download page after confirmation. Install 64-bit Python 3.12, then Find Python again. Manual executable selection is an advanced option; selected files are checked asynchronously. A ready engine hides routine installation controls and offers the next workflow step instead.
  5. Wait for binary-wheel SHA-256 verification, exact package-version, native-import and dependency checks to finish. Start analysis only when the engine is ready.

QGIS's plugin-manager manual describes the Install from ZIP control. Installing the archive normally feels quick because it copies the interface files; it is not the numerical-package installation step.

docs.title: Python choices and readiness
docs.text:
• Checking…: wait for the background check; this does not mean Python is absent.
  • Compatible Python listed: use the recommended choice, then Set up engine. Selecting it installs nothing. Only compatible 64-bit CPython 3.12 choices are listed.
  • No compatible Python found: use Get Python 3.12… for instructions and an explicitly confirmed official-page link, install it, then Find Python again. Python itself is never silently installed by the plugin.
  • Ready to calculate: no setup action is required. Use the next-step button; repair/manual selection live under Manage engine (advanced).
  • Failure: read the inline message and Details. Do not resolve it by installing packages into QGIS. A failed repair keeps a previously verified engine only when that engine remains valid for the current lock.

Install a compatible Python from the official Python releases on Windows. Choose the 64-bit CPython 3.12 installer, not simply the newest Python major/minor version or a Store alias. Manual selection is an advanced recovery route and asynchronously checks the executable before presenting it as compatible.

docs.title: GDAL and other numerical packages
docs.text:
QGIS uses its own geospatial libraries for QGIS work. The separate engine uses the locked Rasterio binary wheel and its native GDAL support, along with locked NumPy/pandas/scikit-learn dependencies. It does not require OSGeo4W's Python GDAL bindings or a global osgeo package injected into the GUI process. Rasterio's installation guide documents the bundled GDAL libraries and the wheels' driver/compatibility limits; the plugin isolates and qualifies its pinned wheels rather than mixing them into QGIS. Native imports and exact installed versions are checked during preparation. Unsupported platforms without the expected wheels fail explicitly; this is not a promise of working on every QGIS/OS/architecture combination.

Setup downloads the locked binary dependencies and needs network access, sufficient disk space and permission to write to the user's QGIS cache. It does not automatically download a Python interpreter. Install Python 3.12 separately from python.org if necessary. On Windows, select python.exe, not pythonw.exe or the Microsoft Store alias.

The initial package installation can take several minutes. You can cancel it from the dialog. A failed or cancelled setup cannot replace a previously verified engine. The setup lock prevents two QGIS processes installing into the same cache concurrently.

docs.title: Update safely
docs.text:
1. Finish the current analysis, or cancel it and wait for the task to stop.
  2. Use Plugins → Manage and Install Plugins → Install from ZIP to install the newly built ZIP. There is no need to uninstall the modern plugin first.
  3. Reopen pypopRF and wait for the engine check. If the packaged dependency lock changed, open Engine → Manage engine (advanced) and choose Repair / update engine, then wait for verification.

For an interface-only update with the same compatible dependency lock, the existing verified engine is reused; downloads are not required merely because the plugin version changed. New engines use shorter unique directory names to reduce Windows path-length failures; already verified legacy environments stay at their original paths and remain reusable. No Windows long-path setting is changed automatically. Your project is separate: select it on Project, click Open project, then verify Project open and Active project: …. Merely choosing the path does not activate it. See Projects.

Analysis and preparation jobs use a private, verified source snapshot and working directory outside the installation. Unloading the plugin requests cancellation; owned resources are released asynchronously after the child actually exits. This protects the installed folder from those jobs, but updating in the middle of an analysis is not a way to preserve or resume that analysis.

The active engine environment switches only after successful verification; old environments are retained for recovery, not recursively deleted. A plugin ZIP replacement and an engine update are different operations. QGIS's ZIP installer does not guarantee rollback for an arbitrary incomplete plugin archive. Use a ZIP built and verified by this repository, and keep the preceding valid ZIP.

Keep analysis projects outside the plugin installation and engine-cache directories. The interface refuses project and preparation destinations inside these protected locations before creating or activating them. This is a location safeguard, not a substitute for backing up an existing legacy installation's data. QGIS manages the installed plugin folder; uninstalling/replacing a plugin is not a project-backup mechanism. Back up the project configuration and important completed runs before changing an installation.

docs.title: One-time migration from a legacy Windows installation
docs.text:
An older plugin may have loaded numerical DLLs from its installation folder into the QGIS process. Disabling the plugin cannot safely unload those DLLs. If this is the installation you are replacing:

  1. In Installed, uncheck pypopRF to disable it; do not uninstall it first.
  2. Save your QGIS project and close all QGIS instances using that profile.
  3. Reopen QGIS with pypopRF still disabled.
  4. Install the valid new ZIP using Install from ZIP, then enable pypopRF.
  5. Set up the separate engine and reopen your analysis project.

Normal QGIS process exit releases the old DLL locks. Do not force-unload DLLs, kill unrelated processes, or manually delete a folder while QGIS still uses it. If replacement still fails, stop and follow the recovery checks.

Existing project input files and earlier run directories are not replaced by an engine update. Model bundles have a strict schema and environment contract; old separate model/scaler files are deliberately not loaded. Retrain when moving to the new engine.

This build does not claim publication in the QGIS repository, automatic self-updates, or offline first-time dependency installation. Do not install dependencies into the QGIS Python environment to work around a setup error; use troubleshooting.

Next: Quick start.

docs.title: Your first population map
docs.text:
This guide takes you from opening pypopRF to a completed population-count map and its saved diagnostics. You supply the study data; the screenshots use small synthetic test data, not a downloadable production dataset.

For ZIP installation and supported platforms, start with Installation. For an existing analysis folder, follow the same workflow but choose Open project instead of creating a new configuration.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
For direct import, have these files ready:

Input What it represents Zone grid A single-band GeoTIFF whose valid pixels contain integer census-zone IDs. Population census A CSV with one row per zone, unique IDs and finite, nonnegative population totals. At least one covariate A single-band numeric GeoTIFF used as a predictor.

The rasters must share CRS, dimensions and the complete pixel transform, including origin and pixel size. Matching CRS alone is not enough. Declare missing data as NoData or valid-data masks. See Input data for the complete contract and optional inputs.

Choose a writable project folder outside the installed plugin and engine/job caches. Keep a backup of the originals: run history is not a backup system. If your data need alignment or polygon rasterization, use the optional preparation route below. Direct import does not silently reproject or resample them.

docs.title: 1. Open Home and choose your next step
docs.text:
Open pypopRF from its QGIS toolbar action or Run Population Modeling menu entry. Home explains the two installation steps and shows current Engine, Project, Inputs and Review/run state.

You can create or open a project before preparing the engine. There is no mandatory startup wizard and a Home action does not automatically start analysis. About / citation… contains packaged authors and the citation for reports.

The Selected for run checklist and Run analysis remain below every tab. They describe selections, not completed scientific validation. Click a checklist item to navigate to its controls.

docs.title: 2. Prepare the separate engine once
docs.text:
Open Engine and wait for the initial background check:

  • Ready to calculate: continue to Project. Routine installation controls are hidden; Manage engine (advanced) is available when needed.
  • Compatible interpreter listed: select it, then choose Set up engine.
  • No compatible interpreter: use Get Python 3.12… for the explicit download-page prompt, install 64-bit CPython 3.12 separately, then choose Find Python again. Advanced manual executable selection is checked before use.

Selecting Python is not installing the engine. Setup creates a private per-user environment and downloads hash-locked packages; wait until verification completes. First setup needs network access and writable cache space. The plugin does not download Python automatically.

Numerical Python/GDAL dependencies run separately from QGIS's Python. Do not install rasterio, NumPy or engine packages into QGIS to bypass an error. See Installation for the isolation and interpreter requirements. A failed repair does not replace a previously verified engine. Read its message and Details; Cancel setup requests cancellation, not successful installation.

docs.title: 3. Create or open the project explicitly
docs.text:
On Project, choose the folder, then use the action next to it:

Folder state Action Result No config.yaml Create project Adds a configuration and project storage; unrelated existing files are not overwritten or automatically selected. Existing config.yaml Open project Validates and restores saved inputs/settings without resetting the configuration. That project is already active Project open (disabled) Activation is complete; a second Open click is unnecessary.

Selecting a folder only chooses a candidate. It does not create/open it. If you choose another folder, explicitly Create/Open it before importing or running. The current-project label and Project readiness item confirm activation.

Create adds config.yaml and the data directory. Activation can also create/append the GUI log under output/; opening does not promise zero filesystem activity. It does not erase inputs or previous runs. If an existing configuration is invalid, keep it and its backup: do not delete it just to make Create appear. See Projects and storage.

docs.title: 4. Select inputs and handle filename conflicts
docs.text:
On Input data:

  1. Select the Zone grid GeoTIFF.
  2. Select the Population census CSV.
  3. Choose Add raster files… to add covariates. Use distinct, meaningful filenames: predictor names come from the files, and informational table cells are read-only.
  4. Wait for each import to finish before the next action.

New files are copied into the project's configured data directory in background jobs; sources are retained. A destination filename collision offers:

  • Use verified existing file, when identical bytes and compatible raster resources have been verified.
  • Import separate copy, under a new portable filename without replacing the old input.
  • Cancel, retaining existing files and configuration.

Do not resolve a conflict by deleting a file whose role you have not checked. A failed selection restores the configured input, not the rejected one. Cancel import requests cancellation of a current copy.

When typing an input path manually, press Enter or Tab to confirm it. A Run click with an uncommitted input confirms the import instead of starting analysis; wait for the import to succeed, then click Run again. Closing discards a draft.

New direct GeoTIFF imports must be self-contained. External .msk, .aux.xml and world-file resources are not silently dropped: read the raster resource rules. Use a QGIS layer… supports underlying local raster files; unsupported remote, memory, filtered or edited layers need an explicit suitable export first.

Optional inputs are Water mask (1 = exclude), Population support (1 = include) and Age and sex census. Their meanings differ. Omit them for a first run unless their support and schema have been checked against the input contract.

docs.title: 5. Map your actual CSV columns and review settings
docs.text:
On Settings → Census columns, enter exact, case-sensitive names:

  • Zone identifier: the column matching integer IDs in the zone grid.
  • Population total: zone population counts, not density.

New projects default to id and pop; the CSV does not need those names. For headers zone_code,total_people, enter zone_code and total_people respectively. Press Tab or leave each field to finish editing. The mapping is saved; source columns are not renamed. An opened project's old mapping is restored, so check it rather than replacing it with defaults.

Begin with conservative processing defaults. Workers/tiles affect resource usage; target transformation and feature selection affect the model. Read Settings before changing them. Add population maps to QGIS controls automatic addition after success.

All checklist items can now look ready. The engine still checks values, ID matching, alignment and eligible support before accepting an analysis.

docs.title: Optional: prepare a separate aligned project
docs.text:
With the engine ready, choose Input data → Prepare / align inputs…:

  1. Choose a Reference raster supplying CRS, extent and resolution. Its values are not an implicit study-area mask. Choose an existing zone ID raster or census polygons to rasterize onto that grid.
  2. Specify CSV ID/population columns and, for polygons, the polygon ID field.
  3. Add predictors with explicit quantity/resampling choices. Continuous measurements, binary indicators and counts have different rules. Counts needing interpolation are refused rather than falsely conserved.
  4. On Review and create, choose an absolute New project directory that does not already exist. Use Check compatibility, read the summary/warnings and acknowledge Create new files; preserve the sources and current project.
  5. Choose Create prepared project. After successful preparation, choose Open prepared project separately to switch to it.

The current project and sources are not updated in place. Changed files/choices require another compatibility check. Add any age-sex CSV after opening the prepared project; it is not automatically migrated. Full restrictions are in Guided preparation.

docs.title: 6. Run and wait for a terminal result
docs.text:
Choose Run analysis. A separate process calculates while QGIS stays responsive. Watch the named stage and elapsed activity, not just percentage: progress is stage-based, not a remaining-time estimate. Details retains full messages when the compact footer shortens them.

Do not edit/regenerate inputs during import or analysis. If preflight fails, read the error, correct data/mapping and run again. An error is not a completed map. Use Stop to request cancellation and wait for stopping to finish. A stopped or failed attempt may leave diagnostics, but source inputs and earlier completed runs are preserved. See Running analysis.

docs.title: 7. Inspect the completed run, not just a colored raster
docs.text:
In Results, select a Complete run. Use Open result folder for artifacts or Add maps to QGIS if automatic addition was off. Maps are grouped by run; adding the same saved map again does not duplicate it. Failed/cancelled attempts are diagnostic history, not finished population products.

Population TIFF values are persons per pixel, not probabilities or people/km². prediction.tif is an allocation-weight surface, not a population-count map. Per-zone census conservation is checked separately from validation; matching supplied totals does not prove the within-zone distribution is accurate.

Read the validation strategy, held-out zone-density diagnostics and limitations. Spatial validation may be unavailable with too few occupied blocks; no score is invented instead. Neither spatial nor shuffled-zone diagnostics establish fine-pixel accuracy. See Validation and scientific limits.

Population in an area… optionally sums a completed map using cell centres inside/on polygon boundaries. Read partial-coverage warnings; it is not area-weighted interpolation or automatically a total for the entire AOI.

docs.title: Reopen or run another analysis
docs.text:
To return later, open pypopRF, select the project folder and choose Open project. Wait for the engine check and review restored paths and CSV mapping. Results → Refresh reads saved history.

For another analysis, deliberately review/change inputs or settings, then Run again. Each accepted attempt uses a fresh <output_dir>/runs/<run_id>/ with its effective configuration and provenance; earlier maps are not replaced. Keep whole run folders when comparing or archiving outputs. See Projects and storage for backup and relocation.

docs.title: Input data
docs.text: An analysis needs one zone grid, a population CSV and at least one numeric raster covariate. Optional inputs are a water mask, a population-support mask and an age/sex CSV. Validation reads inputs and does not rename their columns or rewrite source CSV files.

docs.title: Choose an input workflow
docs.text:
Create or open an external project first; see Projects. Then use Input data:

  • Already aligned data: select the zone grid and census CSV, then Add raster files… in the covariate section. Direct import copies files; it does not align them.
  • Data needing alignment or census polygons: with the engine ready, choose Prepare / align inputs…. Check compatibility and create a new prepared project. The wizard does not repair the current project in place.
  • A layer already in QGIS: choose Use a QGIS layer…, select its role, then the layer. This uses a supported local file source, not an arbitrary live or remote provider. Export unsupported layers first or use preparation.

Selection in the footer is only a checklist. Run analysis performs full numerical validation. A successful copy does not prove that grids, census IDs or predictor support are compatible.

docs.title: Raster grid contract
docs.text:
Use single-band GeoTIFFs with a defined CRS. Mastergrid, covariates and optional masks must have the same CRS, dimensions and complete affine pixel transform: pixel size, origin and rotation all matter. A shifted grid is rejected even if its dimensions match. Small floating-point transform roundoff is tolerated; the engine does not automatically reproject or resample inputs.

For a new GUI import, use a self-contained GeoTIFF. Imports with external mask or georeferencing sidecars such as .msk, .aux.xml, .tfw, .tifw, .wld or .prj are rejected with export guidance rather than silently losing those resources. A complete dataset already inside the project's data directory can be selected in place, keeping its sidecars. The headless engine records GDAL's input resource list, including available sidecars, in run provenance.

NoData and GDAL valid-data masks are respected. Ordinary numeric zero is valid unless the raster declares it NoData. Mark missing data correctly rather than using a finite sentinel as an undeclared measurement.

docs.title: Zone grid
docs.text:
Each valid pixel contains the integer ID of its census zone. An ID occurs in many pixels; pixel values do not have to be globally unique. Gaps outside the study area are allowed when marked NoData. IDs must match the population CSV. IDs must be exactly representable integers within the supported numeric range (absolute value no greater than 2**53).

Zero is a valid zone ID if it is not declared NoData. Numeric IDs such as 1 and 1.0 identify the same zone; text codes such as A001 are not supported. The CSV identifier spelling is checked before floating-point parsing: out-of-range or fractional IDs are rejected, not rounded to a nearby zone. A Python API caller must also preserve its original values; precision already lost before calling the engine cannot be reconstructed.

Every training census zone needs eligible grid pixels and a finite mean for each configured covariate. Zones without that support are reported as errors, including zones whose population is zero. Extra grid IDs without census totals are excluded from population outputs and recorded in diagnostics.

docs.title: Population CSV
docs.text:
Use a CSV with unique, nonempty headers. Map the ID and population columns in Settings; names are case-sensitive and must differ. For example:

id,pop
1,100
2,120
3,0

Save this schema as population.csv and supply a zone raster with IDs 1, 2 and 3. These illustrative numbers are not a downloadable raster dataset or an accuracy benchmark. Even zone 3 needs valid training support.

For a table headed zone_code,people, import it normally, then set Zone identifier to zone_code and Population total to people in Settings. Import does not require the default id/pop names; the engine checks the chosen mapping when Run starts.

IDs must be unique, finite integers. Population totals must be numeric, finite and nonnegative; zero and fractional totals are accepted. Empty tables, duplicate IDs and missing values fail validation. Rows can appear in any order: joins and output checks use zone IDs rather than row positions.

Additional columns are not automatically used as predictors. A nonmissing group column may be retained for explicitly configured grouped validation. Avoid derived column names such as dens, eligible_pixel_count and names used for covariate statistics. A population column named sum is supported without changing the source file.

docs.title: Covariates
docs.text:
Provide aligned single-band numeric rasters. The model trains on each covariate's valid-pixel mean within a zone and predicts from selected covariate values at individual pixels. Pixels lacking any selected predictor receive NoData predictions; they are not filled with arbitrary sentinel values.

Continuous measurements, distances, counts and meaningful binary indicators can be used. Categorical class codes are not encoded automatically: averaging arbitrary land-use codes is not meaningful. Derive appropriate indicators or other numeric representations before supplying categorical information.

Missing covariates can reduce allocation support. A zone with positive population and no positive eligible prediction weight fails instead of losing its population silently. Confirm that the remaining support is appropriate for the study; conserved totals alone do not validate its geographic coverage.

docs.title: Optional masks
docs.text:
The water mask is binary: 1 excludes a pixel and 0 retains it. Masked or NoData mask pixels are also excluded.

The population-support mask is binary: 1 includes a pixel and 0 excludes it from constrained allocation. NoData support pixels are excluded. The engine creates a temporary constrained zone-ID grid while preserving the original zone identifiers. Do not supply a second, unrelated administrative-ID raster as the GUI population-support mask.

An unconstrained population map is always produced. When a support mask is provided, a separate constrained map is produced and checked against the same census totals. The source masks and mastergrid are not modified.

Training uses the mastergrid after water exclusion, not the constrained subset. The constraint limits the additional constrained allocation; it does not silently change the training-density denominator or replace the unconstrained result.

docs.title: Age and sex CSV
docs.text:
Use the configured ID column and the same unique zone-ID set as the main population CSV. Group columns must match the supported complete naming pattern, for example f0, m0, f_0_4, m_5_9, f65+ or m65+. Names are matched case-insensitively; ambiguous duplicate group names are rejected. Unrelated metadata columns are ignored.

Each group contains finite nonnegative totals and is joined by ID. Every group map is checked against that group's supplied totals. The engine does not require the sum of all group columns to equal the main population total. It records a keyed comparison in agesex/age_sex_totals.csv and a bounded mismatch summary in the run manifest. Check that consistency if the columns form a complete demographic partition: a mismatch is diagnostic, not forced rescaling or a hard error. Different row order does not change which zone receives a group.

Both CSVs must contain the Zone identifier column selected in Settings. An age-sex import without that column is refused with an inline explanation; the original file and previous selection are retained. This is not an automatic ID conversion. If one dataset uses IDX and another uses id, first establish whether their values identify the same zones. Different ID systems need a verified correspondence table (crosswalk), applied explicitly to a separate copy. Never pair records by their row order or guess a mapping from similar ID suffixes. Preflight reports missing/extra zone counts and examples before modelling.

For the population example above, a synthetic complete partition could be:

id,f_0_49,m_0_49,f50+,m50+
2,40,40,20,20
1,35,35,15,15
3,0,0,0,0

The reversed row order is intentional. Each row sums to its main population total here, but that relationship is yours to establish. For a partial set of age bands, a mismatch diagnostic may be expected. A regular id,pop census is not silently assigned as an age-sex table; select the optional age-sex role explicitly and supply supported group headers.

docs.title: Guided preparation
docs.text:
The preparation wizard creates a separate new project. Its reference raster is a grid template (CRS, extent, transform and dimensions), not an implicit study-area mask. Zone validity comes from the original zone raster or explicitly chosen census polygons. The tool does not silently clip a whole census polygon to a smaller reference extent and allocate its full population into the remnant.

Follow the wizard's four pages: Source data, Census columns, Predictors and support, and Review and create. Choose either an existing zone-ID raster or census polygons, map the CSV columns explicitly, and choose a new output folder. Use Check compatibility, read errors/warnings and coverage, then confirm Create new files; preserve the sources and current project. Only an accepted compatibility report enables preparation. If a source changes, check again. Choose Create prepared project, then Open prepared project when creation succeeds; add optional age-sex inputs afterward.

Choose predictor quantity and resampling explicitly (1–32 covariates in this guided preparation version):

  • Continuous: nearest, bilinear or average alignment. The choice changes predictor values and must be appropriate for the measurement.
  • Binary indicator / mask: checked 0/1 values with nearest-neighbour alignment. Multiclass category codes must first be encoded as meaningful indicators; averaging arbitrary class numbers is not supported.
  • Count: already-aligned nearest passthrough only. Changing cell size or CRS requires a separately justified conservative aggregation method; this wizard refuses to pretend ordinary interpolation preserves counts.

The derived GeoTIFFs embed the source validity in NaN NoData. Original GDAL resources, CSV and vector resources are fingerprinted, rechecked, and retained unchanged. Diagnostics include zone-ID matching, grid changes, missing support, joint predictor coverage, warnings and a full coverage CSV. Review the report before committing preparation. Unsupported or invalid data are not automatically repaired. Census vectors and tables are materialized and must fit engine memory; this is not a streaming vector ETL pipeline. Geographic coordinates and spans that require antimeridian splitting are refused before or after reprojection. Split/export them explicitly; the wizard does not guess a dateline repair. The GUI binds preparation to the inspected source hashes. A changed CSV, raster or sidecar requires a new compatibility check, not reuse of the old confirmation.

Existing project files with external masks can be prepared into self-contained GeoTIFFs; direct GUI copy still rejects sidecars to avoid losing them. The prepared project includes a compatible config.yaml, derived data, report and provenance. After a late cancellation or forced stop, a newly requested output folder may remain. The message identifies a retained folder; treat it as potentially incomplete, inspect it separately and choose a new destination for retry. Cancellation never silently deletes or overwrites it.

Age-sex inputs are added after opening the prepared project; this first wizard does not automatically copy a previously configured age-sex table. The original project retains it. Preparation is deliberately conservative: lack of jointly valid predictor support is diagnosed rather than resolved by implicit imputation.

docs.title: Direct file import
docs.text:
New files are copied in cancellable background jobs into the project's data directory, normally <project>/data/. When typing a path manually, complete it and press Enter, Tab or leave the field to commit it. Enter confirms only that input, never Run or Cancel. If you click Run analysis with an uncommitted input path, that click commits the import first; wait for success and click Run analysis again. It does not calculate from the previous input. Intermediate keystrokes do not start imports; closing the dialog discards an uncommitted draft. Browsing still commits the selected path immediately. Existing destination names are never overwritten. A conflict dialog explains the selected role and offers:

  • Use verified existing file only when source/destination bytes match and raster sidecars do not make byte-only reuse unsafe.
  • Import separate copy under a new portable basename with the same extension. For example, elevation_copy.tif, not a folder path.
  • Cancel, retaining the previous input selection and both files.

Hashing runs in the worker, not the GUI. A choice is rechecked before reuse or publication; changed sources/destinations are refused. A new-name collision also fails instead of overwriting. Selecting the ordinary canonical file already in the data directory reuses it in place, retaining its GDAL resources. File-symlink aliases and hardlinked existing collision targets are refused; select the canonical dedicated file or export a separate copy.

Incomplete copies are staged and not registered. Clearing an optional file field or removing a covariate from the table removes only its configuration reference, not the physical file. Every new copied import verifies the source snapshot, staged bytes and current source before publication, even without a name conflict. This adds background reads but never installs packages or hashes on the GUI thread. Keep source files stable throughout import and analysis; this is change detection, not an adversarial point-in-time snapshot of another writer.

Projects · Settings · Run an analysis

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
The current interface has seven tabs: Home, Engine, Project, Input data, Settings, Results and Details. Historical screenshots from earlier plugin versions do not describe this layout.

The plugin uses one independent light color scheme: white surfaces, dark text, blue actions/selection and explicit semantic errors. It does not inherit QGIS's dark/gray theme or change the appearance of QGIS and other plugins. All plugin dialogs use this scheme; native operating-system file pickers remain controlled by the operating system. User fonts and display scaling are respected.

The compact Selected for run checklist sits below the tabs, beside the persistent run/status area, and is visible from every tab. Engine, Project, Zone grid, Census and Covariates show selection readiness; click an item to navigate to its existing controls. These checks do not replace the engine's scientific validation of grid alignment, census IDs or data support.

Task text appears in a separate plain-text status area, fitted to at most three rendered lines so long messages cannot push the run action off-screen. A tooltip retains the caller-bounded text; Details contains the full diagnostics and Copy diagnostics copies the displayed messages. Elapsed stage text is fitted to two rendered lines. The numeric progress bar is shown during analysis/import/tools work and hidden when idle. Failures remain visible after readiness refresh; Details opens the complete diagnostics when a long message is shortened. Engine setup also has its own progress on the Engine tab.

docs.title: Home
docs.text: Home shows the packaged project logo, the two installation steps and a next action based on current readiness. Guidance can be collapsed; readiness is always recomputed, not remembered as a stale completed step. Projects remain usable without an engine for inspection; calculations and preparation require it. About / citation… shows packaged authors, version, links and citation. Links open only when explicitly clicked.

docs.title: Engine
docs.text:
The Engine tab checks for the plugin's isolated Python runtime. Checking, missing Python, verified selection, preparation, readiness and failure have distinct visible states. A ready engine offers the next workflow step instead of installation controls. Manage engine (advanced) reveals repair, discovery and manual interpreter selection; downloading Python is offered only when needed. Choose a verified 64-bit CPython 3.12 from the discovery list and use Set up engine when needed. Setup downloads the locked wheel dependencies into a separate per-user environment; plugin activation does not install packages into QGIS. An update only switches to a verified new environment after its checks pass.

Setup and discovery run in a background worker. Cancel setup requests cancellation of setup. Read the readiness message to see whether a project, inputs or engine preparation is still needed. See the installation guide for platform details.

docs.title: Project
docs.text:
Choose a folder outside the plugin/cache, then explicitly activate it:

Folder state Action / state What it means Nothing selected Choose project folder (disabled) Select a folder first. Selected folder has no config.yaml Create project Add a new configuration and project data directory; unrelated files are not imported or overwritten. Selected folder contains config.yaml Open project Validate and restore saved inputs/settings. Successfully active folder Project open (disabled) Ready for input/settings work; repeated clicks do not reload the project.

Active project: … identifies the folder actually opened. Merely selecting a different folder does not activate it: input/settings controls and Run are gated until you explicitly create/open that selection. Selecting the same active path does not invalidate the project. Open folder opens the active project's directory in your file manager; it does not activate a new selection.

Opening preserves the saved configuration and earlier runs, although the GUI may create or append its diagnostic log. Locations are checked before activation, imports, analysis and log switching. The GUI log stays in the project's output folder even when numerical output_dir differs; dedicated regular log files are required. Refused locations are not moved or deleted. See Projects for folder layout, switching, movement and backup rules.

docs.title: Input data
docs.text:
Select the Zone grid and Population census and add at least one covariate using Add raster files…. Optional fields are Water mask (1 = exclude), Population support (1 = include) and Age and sex census.

Imports run outside the GUI and report progress. Filename conflicts open a choice to reuse verified identical bytes (with raster-resource checks), import a separate copy under a new name, or cancel. Existing inputs are never overwritten. Clearing a field removes its configuration reference, not the copied file. CSV headers are previewed, but column mapping and numerical checks still occur before analysis. The run button becomes Cancel import while an import is active. Destination names are checked; inputs are not overwritten. On a failed selection the field is restored to the input actually configured in the project.

The covariate table shows name, size, path and actions. Its informational cells are read-only. Use a row's Delete button or the Delete key to remove selected covariates from configuration; their copied files remain in the data directory. See input requirements for alignment, NoData and sidecar rules.

Prepare / align inputs… opens a guided workflow using the separate numerical engine. Select a reference grid, an existing zone raster or census polygons, CSV ID/population columns, and explicit predictor quantities/resampling methods. Inspect the diagnostics and acknowledge the choices before creating a new prepared project. Existing projects and source files are not overwritten. The wizard opens the prepared project only after successful completion and your confirmation. See preparation rules.

Local QGIS layers can be selected instead of browsing for supported raster/vector files. These controls use the underlying local dataset, not rendered colors. Remote, memory, virtual, filtered or edited layers must be explicitly exported first; a selection is not silently substituted for the complete file.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Map census column names, configure workers and tile size, choose the target transform and feature-selection threshold, and set diagnostic logging. The option Add population maps to QGIS applies after successful completion. There is no model-import control or GUI control for advanced spatial-CV settings.

Full descriptions and supported advanced YAML fields are in Settings.

docs.title: Running and stopping
docs.text:
The prominent Run analysis action stays below every tab. Its appearance does not bypass readiness checks; it changes to the appropriate cancellation action during owned work. Run analysis starts a separate engine process. Numerical preflight, fingerprinting, fitting and raster computation occur outside the QGIS GUI. The progress area names the current stage; numerical stage percentages are milestones rather than an estimate of remaining wall-clock time.

Stop requests cooperative cancellation. If the owned calculation process does not respond within the grace period, the adapter stops that process. The GUI waits for native process completion before releasing job ownership or presenting a terminal result. Closing or unloading during background work requests cancellation and defers disposal until owned work has finished. Earlier runs remain available.

docs.title: Results
docs.text:
Each attempt has its own directory beneath <output_dir>/runs/. The Results tab lists recent runs with status and population-map count. Use Refresh, Open result folder, or Add maps to QGIS. Only complete runs with valid, present population-map paths can be added. Failed, running or cancelled attempts can be inspected for diagnostics but are not treated as finished maps. Run timestamps are displayed in local time; the original directory ID remains in the tooltip. Refresh preserves your selected run, while a newly successful analysis selects its own results rather than a newer failed attempt.

The raw prediction.tif contains model density weights and is not added as a population-count result. The result folder also contains the effective config, model bundle, extracted features, validation records and manifest.

The quality dashboard below the run history reads the saved held-out zone-density predictions, not the final census-normalized map. It shows OOF observed/predicted scatter, highest absolute zone-density errors, permutation importance and explicit validation limitations. The training-mean baseline uses the same outer folds and only the other folds' observations. Missing, changed or unsupported diagnostic artifacts are reported rather than replaced by made-up scores. Conservation remains a separate engine-reported check; this panel does not independently recompute raster totals or establish pixel accuracy.

Show selected / top error zones in QGIS adds diagnostic zone-centre points when saved centroids and CRS are available. Those points identify census zones, not the location of pixel errors. Completed population maps are grouped by run under pypopRF, with log-spaced display colors and persons/pixel labels; styles do not alter values. Re-adding the same result does not duplicate it.

Population in an area… sums a selected completed population map inside a local polygon AOI. The rule is cell centre inside or on the polygon boundary; overlapping AOI polygons are unioned and counted once. Cells partly intersecting the boundary are not fractionally allocated. Coverage is the fraction of selected centres within the raster with valid values, not the fraction of the entire AOI area. An AOI outside the raster or containing NoData yields a clearly labelled partial supported-cell sum. This is a model-derived estimate, not a new census.

docs.title: Details
docs.text:
The activity area shows the actual current message and elapsed time, not an ETA. Package downloading uses an indeterminate indicator rather than a false byte percentage. Details includes a bounded stage history, and opening a project or starting a calculation does not clear earlier diagnostic messages.

Details shows bounded plain-text setup and processing messages. Clear view clears the displayed messages; Copy diagnostics copies them for a bug report. Clearing the view does not delete saved logs or previous runs.

Verification of zone totals checks allocation arithmetic. It does not establish where people actually live within a zone; reported model scores describe held-out zone-average density rather than independent pixel-level accuracy.

Quick start · Running analysis

docs.title: Projects and storage
docs.text: A pypopRF project is an analysis folder, not the installed plugin or the QGIS .qgz project. It stores settings, imported data and independent runs. A QGIS project can reference its maps, but cannot replace a backup of those files.

docs.title: Select, then activate
docs.text:
On Project, selection and activation are different:

State Button Meaning No folder selected Unavailable Choose an external folder. Selected folder has no config.yaml Create project Adds a configuration; unrelated existing files are retained. Selected folder contains config.yaml Open project Validates and restores the saved configuration. Selected folder is already active Project open (disabled) Activation is complete; no repeated Open is needed.

Choosing another folder makes it a candidate, not an active replacement. Explicitly Create/Open it before importing or running. The current-project label and Project readiness item identify the active folder; Open folder opens its location in the system file manager. Project inspection does not require the engine; analysis and guided preparation do.

docs.title: New and existing folders
docs.text:
Create works in a new folder or an existing external folder without config.yaml. It adds the configuration and data directory; it does not rename, delete or replace unrelated files or automatically register them as inputs. Select appropriate existing files explicitly.

If config.yaml exists, open it. Do not delete it to force Create or replace it with an example merely because inputs are incomplete. Open reads/validates it without resetting CSV mappings, predictor names or settings. Subsequent explicit input/settings changes are saved; opening itself does not rewrite YAML.

Activation can create/append GUI diagnostics under output/. Thus configuration read-only opening is not a promise that the whole folder is untouched. Existing ordinary GUI logs append/rotate rather than truncate.

Project, configured data/output and GUI log locations must stay outside the plugin installation and engine/job caches. An unsafe-location error does not move/delete data: back it up and relocate the complete project yourself.

docs.title: Default storage
docs.text:
study-project/
├── config.yaml                 current selections and settings
├── data/                       scientific inputs
└── output/
    ├── logs_pypoprf.log         GUI diagnostics, default filename
    └── runs/
        └── <run_id>/           one analysis attempt
            ├── manifest.json
            ├── run_config.yaml
            ├── population_unconstrained.tif
            └── ...            model, validation and other artifacts

A newly created project has no completed run. Failed/cancelled attempts may contain diagnostics or partial artifacts, not final maps.

data_dir and output_dir can differ, including absolute paths. The GUI log still uses <project>/output/, independently of analysis output_dir. See Settings. Include configured external locations when backing up or moving.

The current configuration is not an earlier run's provenance: each run saves its effective run_config.yaml, fingerprints and manifest. Keep the complete run folder, not just the TIFF, when you need to explain or reproduce an output.

docs.title: Inputs and history are not silently overwritten
docs.text:
Imports are staged in background jobs and registered after successful copy. A filename collision requires verified reuse, a separately named copy, or Cancel. Identical bytes alone are insufficient when raster resources are incompatible. See Quick start and Input data.

Clearing a field or deleting a covariate row removes the configuration reference, not the copied file. The plugin does not recursively clean the data directory. Re-running retains earlier runs; Stop is not an instruction to erase source data or historical results.

Prepare / align inputs… creates a separate new project and derived inputs. Open prepared project is an explicit later switch; the previous project remains available. Add age-sex data after opening the prepared project, since the wizard does not automatically migrate every optional file.

docs.title: Back up and move safely
docs.text:
1. Finish or Stop owned work and wait for it to end. Before editing configuration externally or moving the folder, save your QGIS project and close QGIS instances using those files: a hidden dialog can retain its logger and pending settings, and loaded raster layers can retain file handles.
  2. Back up config.yaml, input resources and complete run folders you need. Include external configured directories and raster sidecars.
  3. Copy/move the whole project to another safe external folder, not inside the plugin installation or engine cache.
  4. Select the new location in pypopRF and choose Open project. Check displayed input paths, CSV mappings and available Results before running.
  5. Correct genuine external/absolute references in a backed-up configuration or explicitly reselect inputs. Verify relocation before removing the old copy yourself.

Relative default data/ and output/ follow the selected folder in the GUI. Opening a moved folder does not rewrite stored work_dir; GUI analysis uses the active selected root for its new snapshot. If you use the headless API/CLI too, check its configured work_dir and external paths separately. Earlier saved run configurations retain their original provenance paths.

New run output names use portable / separators. Results also accepts legacy Windows backslash separators for contained relative paths, so nested age-sex maps remain visible after a Windows-to-Linux move. Drive/UNC paths, traversal and files outside the run are still refused. This does not rewrite old input/provenance paths.

QGIS layers can still point to old files. Add the relocated project's completed maps through Results → Add maps to QGIS, or update the QGIS project deliberately; moving the folder does not rewrite .qgz layer sources automatically.

docs.title: Older configurations and CSV mappings
docs.text:
Compatible saved configurations retain their mappings. For example, census_id_column: zone_code and census_pop_column: total_people refer to those exact CSV headers, not defaults id/pop. Named covariates entries and filenames must also remain meaningful. Review Settings → Census columns after opening; the plugin does not rename the table.

Older/manually edited YAML may lack required fields or contain invalid types. Not every historical configuration is automatically converted. Keep the original folder/configuration and read the error in Details. See Settings for supported fields. If compatibility is uncertain, create a separate clean project, explicitly select/import verified data, and re-enter their mappings; do not destroy the old folder to make the new interface accept it. Legacy separate model/scaler files are not a shortcut around retraining.

Each new analysis records its own settings and inputs. Completion/conserved totals do not replace reviewing validation and support: see Validation and scientific limits.

docs.title: Run an analysis and interpret its results
docs.text: Use an open external project, compatible input data and reviewed settings. Every attempt creates a separate run; it does not replace an earlier population map.

docs.title: From project to Run
docs.text:
1. On Engine, wait for the engine check to finish. If it is not prepared, choose a compatible Python and Set up engine. A ready engine needs no routine repair before each analysis. You can open a project without an installed engine once background work has finished, but cannot calculate yet.
  2. On Project, create/open the intended folder. Selecting a different folder makes it a candidate and disables Run/input editing until you explicitly open it. The candidate is not activated and the previous saved project is not overwritten just by changing the selection.
  3. On Input data, select a zone grid and population census, and use Add raster files… for at least one named covariate. Finish any copy/conflict dialog or preparation first. Optional masks and age-sex counts must obey their distinct input contracts.
  4. On Settings, check the CSV column mapping, tile/worker budget and target transform. On the footer, review Selected for run, then choose Run analysis. Run is disabled when required selections/engine are missing. While another task owns the interface, starting a new run is refused; the same main control may instead offer Stop/Cancel for that task.

The checklist describes selected inputs, not their numerical validity. The separate engine checks CSV schema and values, full raster alignment, validity masks and eligible census support before publishing population maps. Selecting a raster does not cause an implicit reprojection/resampling; use Prepare / align inputs… deliberately if needed.

Keep project configuration, CSVs, rasters and sidecars stable during import or analysis. Fingerprints detect observed resource changes, not an adversarial point-in-time snapshot of another process repeatedly replacing/restoring data. Calculating raster statistics in QGIS or another GDAL application can create an .aux.xml sidecar. Do that before Run, not during calculation: adding a resource changes the input snapshot and the attempt is rejected rather than silently accepted with different provenance.

docs.title: What runs, and how to stop it
docs.text:
The workflow applies water exclusion, derives any constrained zone grid, extracts zonal covariate means, trains/validates the seeded Random Forest, predicts nonnegative weights and redistributes census totals over eligible pixels. The main map is always unconstrained; a supplied support mask adds a separately normalized constrained map. Age-sex maps use ID-keyed totals for each supported group, not CSV row positions.

While calculating, the main action becomes Stop. It requests cooperative cancellation without blocking the GUI. The interface retains the owned child and temporary files until actual process exit is verified. After the grace period, an unresponsive owned process may be stopped forcibly; unrelated Python or QGIS processes are not targeted. Closing/unloading follows the same ownership rule. Engine setup has its own Cancel setup action on Engine; cancelling a check is not the same as a failed engine verification.

The footer shows compact status and elapsed task time. Long messages are fitted to a few painted lines; their complete caller-bounded text remains in the tooltip and Details. The Details page holds full diagnostic messages and stage history. Progress milestones are not an ETA, a download-byte percentage or an accuracy score. Engine package downloads use an indeterminate activity bar.

Output files are published individually from temporary files after successful close/validation. A stopped or failed run can retain intermediate files for diagnosis, but that is not a complete result. Its terminal manifest records failure/cancellation; an attempt rejected before creating a run may have no history entry. Previous runs and source files are preserved.

docs.title: Find the saved run
docs.text:
Open Results and select a run. Refresh rereads history without discarding your selection. Open result folder opens its files; Add maps to QGIS loads population maps from a completed run. Failed/stopped attempts remain available for diagnosis, not map loading. A newly verified successful run takes selection; a failed attempt does not silently replace the selected earlier run. An existing run with malformed metadata or missing/unsafe outputs is shown as Invalid, not Complete. Its folder remains available for diagnosis; map loading and population summaries stay disabled until the data are repaired.

Default location:

<project>/output/runs/<timestamp-id>/

If output_dir differs, use <output_dir>/runs/<timestamp-id>/. Run IDs are shown as local start times in Results; the exact ID/path is in the row tooltip.

Product Use manifest.json Status, displayable outputs, input/resource fingerprints, artifact inventory, runtime/source provenance and diagnostics. run_config.yaml All effective settings/defaults and resolved input paths. population_unconstrained.tif Final estimated persons per pixel on unconstrained valid support. population_constrained.tif Additional persons-per-pixel map when a support mask was supplied. prediction.tif Model allocation weights; not final population counts. normalized_census*.tif Zone normalization coefficients, not a population map. agesex/population_<group>*.tif Group-specific population maps, optionally constrained. agesex/age_sex_totals.csv ID-keyed demographic-sum versus main-census comparison. features.csv Derived zonal training table, not a rewritten source census. cv_metrics.json, cv_predictions.csv, cv_zone_geometry.csv Actual held-out validation, folds and spatial diagnostics. feature_importance.csv Final training procedure's permutation selection scores/spread. model_bundle.pkl.gz Model/preprocessing/schema bundle; executable serialization, trusted sources only. Configured .log file Engine diagnostics for this run, if file logging is enabled.

The manifest's displayable outputs list differs from its complete immutable artifact inventory. Mutable logs and the manifest itself are not included in that inventory. A file being present does not establish that its run completed; the GUI requires consistent terminal status and verified output metadata.

docs.title: Read the quality dashboard
docs.text:
Selecting a saved run loads the dashboard beneath history. Keep two questions separate:

  • Conservation: did redistribution match each supplied census zone/group total within numerical tolerances? This is a correctness check, not evidence that people were located correctly within the zone. The dashboard reports the engine's recorded conservation result; opening history does not rerun every per-zone raster sum.
  • Held-out density quality: how well did the complete training procedure predict census-zone average density on held-out zones? The observed/predicted scatter uses out-of-fold predictions, not in-sample fitting or independent pixel observations.

Inspect RMSE, MAE, R² where available, the validation strategy/limits, high-error zones and feature selection scores. A displayed mean baseline is derived from the other folds' training targets, not the held-out target itself. Missing, malformed or inconsistent saved artifacts make diagnostics unavailable rather than producing invented points or trustworthy-looking scores.
