Show selected / top error zones in QGIS adds diagnostic centroid markers when saved spatial geometry/CRS is available. They are zone-centroid locations, not zone-boundary polygons or a pixel-confidence surface. Inspect them alongside your administrative boundaries and source data.

Default spatial validation divides the full raster footprint into a 4×4 grid and assigns eligible zone-pixel centroids to blocks. All zones within a block stay together; preprocessing/selection/forest are freshly fitted inside each outer training fold. There is no separation buffer: large zones may cross block boundaries and adjacent blocks may remain dependent. Too few occupied blocks makes metrics unavailable, with no hidden shuffled fallback. User groups and shuffled-zone diagnostics are explicitly labelled. See advanced validation settings before comparing block designs.

The density target and RMSE/MAE use population per eligible mastergrid pixel, not people/km²; R² and normalized errors are dimensionless. None validates high-resolution accuracy. Changing blocks, support, grid resolution or target transform can change the comparison. Use independent data and a justified spatial design before making fine-pixel accuracy claims.

docs.title: Estimate population inside an AOI
docs.text:
1. Select a completed run in Results with the engine ready and no other task running, then choose Population in an area….
  2. Choose a published population map and local polygon file/QGIS layer. Do not use prediction.tif, coefficients or an unrelated density raster.
  3. Choose Calculate population and read both the total and coverage warning. During calculation, Stop requests cancellation; closing also waits for the owned operation to stop.

The tool unions overlapping polygons so cells are counted once, transforms valid polygon geometry into the raster CRS and sums finite supported cell counts. A cell is included when its center is inside or on the polygon boundary. There is no fractional boundary-cell allocation or area-weighted interpolation.

The displayed estimate is rounded to whole persons; it is still a model estimate. Coverage is valid cells divided by selected raster cell centers, not the fraction of the AOI's physical area. An AOI extending beyond the raster or containing unsupported cells is reported as partial coverage, not an entire-AOI total. No selected centers gives no evidence of zero population. Invalid/empty geometry is rejected, not silently repaired.

When the selected run provides an artifact SHA-256, the tool checks the population raster against it before summing. Legacy results without a saved fingerprint carry an explicit integrity warning. The summary dialog displays the result; it does not rewrite the raster or append an AOI total to the immutable run.

docs.title: Reproduce or diagnose a run
docs.text:
Keep run_config.yaml, manifest.json, inputs including GDAL sidecars, and the runtime/source version information together. Input resources are fingerprinted and rechecked before completion. The GUI launches a verified private code snapshot in a separate job directory; replacing plugin files later does not change that already-started child. This is not a copy/snapshot of all input data. Direct engine CLI runs record live_source when no verified code snapshot is supplied; the manifest distinguishes that origin explicitly.

Fixed seeds help repeat a given environment/input/validation design, but do not promise bitwise equivalence across changed libraries, platforms or data. Recorded effective defaults prevent silently adopting later defaults. The GUI does not load/reuse model bundles; API reuse rejects incompatible environment/grid contracts and accepts only trusted serialization. A compatible load is not a scientific guarantee about transfer to another region.

For a failed run, read the final error in Details and inspect its manifest/log before changing inputs. Positive-population zones without positive eligible allocation weight fail; zero-population zones remain zero. Raster-only zones without census records are excluded and diagnosed. Age-sex totals are conserved per input group; their sum is compared with, not forcibly rescaled to, the main census. Fix the underlying support/schema issue rather than treating missing validation or a stopped run as success.

Projects · Input requirements · Settings · Troubleshooting

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: Settings are saved in the project's config.yaml. Opening a project restores its existing configuration. Every analysis also saves run_config.yaml with all effective defaults and canonical input paths, so a later default change does not silently change the recorded settings of an earlier run.

docs.title: Set up a first run
docs.text:
1. Open the intended project and finish any import/compatibility checks in Input data.
  2. In Settings, enter the exact CSV Zone identifier and Population total names. For zone_code,people, use zone_code and people; there is no automatic renaming of your source columns. The optional age-sex table uses the same identifier name.
  3. Keep the default log transform and selection threshold for a first test unless your study design justifies a change. Start with a modest worker budget; leave raster tiling enabled.
  4. Review the selection checklist, then use Run analysis in the footer. It still validates the actual files and support in the separate engine.

Controls save project configuration; opening an existing project restores its values rather than replacing them with new-project defaults. Do not change configuration or inputs while an import, preparation or calculation is running.

docs.title: Controls in the Settings tab
docs.text: Control New project default Meaning Zone identifier id Exact CSV column name containing zone IDs. Population total pop Exact CSV column containing nonnegative population totals. Use multiple CPU cores Off Off uses one worker; on uses the selected worker count. CPU cores 1 in the saved new-project configuration Shared worker budget for supported raster operations and RF fitting. Process raster tiles in parallel On Enables tile processing for zonal extraction and allocation. Tile size 512,512 Width and height in pixels; GUI choices are 256, 512 and 1024 square tiles. Use log-transformed population density On Fits log1p(density) and converts predictions with expm1. Feature selection threshold 0.01 Threshold for normalized holdout permutation importance. Add population maps to QGIS On Adds verified population maps after successful completion. Detail level INFO Selects the amount of diagnostic logging. Log filename logs_pypoprf.log A plain .log filename, without directories or reserved device names.

docs.title: Target, selection and resource use
docs.text:
The target density is population divided by the number of eligible mastergrid pixels in each census zone. It does not depend on the ordering of covariates. It is not a value in people/km² unless a separate unit conversion is performed. Water-excluded/invalid grid pixels are not eligible. The optional constraint limits the additional constrained population output, not this training target.

Feature importance is an increase in validation RMSE, normalized by the larger of the training target standard deviation and mean absolute target. It is not a probability or a cumulative share of features. If the threshold excludes every useful feature, the best positive feature is retained. With no credible positive ranking, a constant target or a very small training subset, all features are retained. Selection is fitted within each outer training fold.

Permutation selection uses an inner holdout and the current training target scale: log1p(density) when the log option is on, raw density when off. Do not compare importance magnitudes across transform choices as though they were the same raw-density score. Outer CV metrics, by contrast, are computed after inversion in raw population-per-eligible-pixel density units.

Both processing modes read bounded raster tiles. Disabling parallel tile processing selects serial execution; it does not request a full-grid read. Prediction also writes tiled windows. Worker count and tile dimensions affect resource usage. Using every CPU does not necessarily improve speed. The owned engine child caps native BLAS/OpenMP pools to one thread each, preventing an extra native pool per RF worker. This does not change the configured RF worker budget or the QGIS host's environment; the run manifest records loaded native pool counts.

docs.title: Advanced configuration
docs.text:
The following fields are supported in config.yaml but do not currently have dedicated GUI controls. Finish or cancel plugin work and wait until it is idle, save any other QGIS work, then exit QGIS before editing the file. Reopen QGIS and explicitly open the project afterward. Merely closing the plugin dialog hides a reused window; opening its already-active folder again may be a no-op, so that is not a reliable external-config reload.

Add/change these fields in the existing project configuration. This snippet is not a replacement for its input paths, column mapping and other settings.

random_seed: 42
n_estimators: 500
cv_folds: 5
cv_strategy: spatial
spatial_grid: [4, 4]
cv_group_column: null

spatial_grid contains the number of columns and rows of spatial blocks over the full mastergrid footprint. It is a subdivision count, not a distance in metres. Valid-pixel zone centroids determine block membership. All zones in a block remain together in external cross-validation; scaler, selection and forest are refitted on training data only.

Raster Tile size is an I/O/resource setting; spatial_grid is a validation design. Changing one does not define the other. cv_folds requests at most that many outer folds; the engine reduces it to the number of available groups/zones.

The default spatial strategy records CRS, pixel/native-unit block dimensions, centroids and limitations. It uses no separation buffer. Large zones can cross the boundaries of their centroid's block, and adjacent blocks can contain dependent observations. Choose the subdivision scale for the study rather than interpreting the default as an estimated autocorrelation distance.

groups uses a nonmissing census cv_group_column or groups supplied to the Python API. Supplied groups are kept together but are not automatically called spatial validation. shuffled_zone is an explicitly labelled diagnostic split which ignores spatial dependence. When spatial CV has fewer than two occupied blocks, or a training zone has no eligible centroid, metrics are unavailable with an explanation; there is no automatic random fallback.

Keep cv_group_column: null for automatic spatial blocking. A configured group column or explicit Python-API groups take precedence over automatic blocking; they are labelled user-supplied grouping, not automatically spatial validation. For example, with a nonmissing district_group census column:

cv_strategy: groups
cv_group_column: district_group

That column is metadata for splitting, not an extra raster predictor. Justify the grouping scientifically; a shared administrative label alone does not prove independence.

The run's cv_metrics.json, cv_predictions.csv and cv_zone_geometry.csv record the actual validation. Scores describe held-out zone-average density, not independent fine-pixel accuracy. Compare candidate models only under the same explicitly recorded folds and support rules; a single block partition is not a general fine-pixel accuracy benchmark.

RMSE and MAE summarize pooled out-of-fold zone-density errors. Normalized RMSE and MAE divide those errors by the mean observed density and are unavailable when that mean is zero. R² is unavailable for a constant observed target; a negative R² can occur. An unavailable score does not authorize changing to a random split merely to obtain a number. With few zones/blocks, interpret any available score cautiously.

docs.title: Paths, logs and model files
docs.text:
data_dir and output_dir are resolved against work_dir; absolute paths are also supported. The GUI creates each run beneath <output_dir>/runs/<run_id>/. Earlier runs are preserved.

The GUI has a separate diagnostic logger. The engine writes its log into the current run. Logs append and rotate rather than truncating previous content. The headless configuration accepts logging.file: null to disable engine file logging; the GUI currently expects a filename.

GUI diagnostics use <project>/output/<Log filename>, even if a different analysis output_dir is configured. Each engine run uses its own log in the run folder. Keep log destinations as dedicated ordinary files; aliases/hardlinks and paths inside plugin/engine/job-cache folders are refused.

The fitted model, scaler, feature order, target transform, versions and training pixel-geometry contract are saved together in model_bundle.pkl.gz. The GUI does not offer model reuse or import. The Python API rejects legacy standalone model/scaler pairs and incompatible bundle environments or grids; retraining is required. Joblib bundles are executable Python serialization and must only be loaded from trusted sources.

The saved grid contract includes CRS and linear affine pixel geometry: a changed resolution/rotation changes the meaning of population per eligible pixel. A compatible bundle load is not evidence that transfer to new geography is accurate.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Start with the status shown in the analysis window. Each attempt has its own directory under output/runs; failed and cancelled attempts never replace a previous completed result. Include the run's log and manifest.json when reporting an issue. Avoid sending personal census data publicly.

docs.title: Start with the symptom
docs.text: What you see First safe action Project shows Open/Create even though a folder was chosen Selection is not activation. Click the action and look for Project open / Active project. Project open is disabled Normal: that folder is already active. Choose a different folder to switch, not repeatedly reopen it. Run analysis is disabled Use the bottom checklist to find the missing engine, active project or required input; green selection checks do not guarantee numerical validity. No compatible Python / requires 64-bit CPython 3.12 Follow Engine's compatible choices or Get Python instructions, then Find Python again. Repair failed, previous engine remains available Read the inline error and Details; do not delete the working environment. Import would overwrite an existing input Resolve the nonmodal reuse / separate-copy / cancel choice, not filesystem deletion. An input field became empty or restored its old value Read its inline error and Details; a rejected import is not registered as a new input. Waiting / Stopping… Wait for owned work to finish; no terminal result is accepted before process completion. Existing folders cannot be opened Check config.yaml, the selected location and configured data/output/log paths; do not create a replacement config over the original.

docs.title: Project selection and activation
docs.text:
The folder picker is only a candidate. A successful Create project or Open project changes the button to Project open (disabled) and shows Active project: … below the picker. Changing the selected folder gates inputs/settings and analysis until that selection is explicitly activated. Selecting the same canonical active folder does not reset it. See Projects.

If opening fails, retain the original config.yaml and inputs. Read the exact error before editing a backup copy. Malformed YAML, missing required saved settings and protected/log-alias locations are refused, not silently repaired. The plugin does not create a compatible project merely by selecting any old data folder or replace a malformed configuration with defaults.

Before editing configuration externally, finish work, save your QGIS project, close QGIS and back up the configuration. After editing, reopen QGIS and explicitly open the analysis folder again. Closing only the plugin dialog hides and reuses it; it does not reread YAML. Project open is a state indicator, not a reload button. Do not change live configuration files while importing or calculating.

docs.title: Import conflicts and cleared references
docs.text: An existing filename can refer to an earlier copied input even after its field was cleared. Clearing a field or deleting a covariate row removes the saved reference, not its file. The conflict dialog offers verified identical-file reuse when eligible, a separate copy with a new name, or cancellation. A byte difference or external raster resources can make reuse unavailable. Never delete an original file just to dismiss the conflict; inspect the choice and input rules.

docs.title: Appearance and lengthy messages
docs.text:
Plugin windows use an independent light scheme even when QGIS is dark. Operating system file pickers/title bars remain operating-system controlled. At a small window size, tab contents may need scrolling; the bottom checklist/status/actions stay accessible. Increase the window size if you use large fonts.

Status text is fitted to three rendered lines; hover for caller-bounded text or open Details for diagnostics. Copy diagnostics copies the displayed log, and Clear view affects that view, not saved files or completed results.

docs.title: Engine setup
docs.text: The interface does not need NumPy, pandas, rasterio or scikit-learn installed in QGIS. Select a compatible 64-bit CPython 3.12 on Engine and use Set up engine. QGIS 4 may use Python 3.13; that interpreter is not the calculation engine. Setup uses a separate cache and exact packaged dependency lock. Check proxy, network, free space and write permissions if package downloads fail. Setup output is shown in Details. Do not run pip in the QGIS Python to work around the failure. An earlier healthy engine remains active if a repair fails; an outdated lock requires successful setup before the new plugin can run.

docs.title: Plugin update or locked folder
docs.text:
Keep a valid previous ZIP and keep projects outside the plugin installation and engine cache. For a legacy plugin which loaded DLLs into QGIS, use the disable → close QGIS → reopen disabled → install ZIP migration. Do not uninstall first or force-delete an active plugin folder.

If installation still fails, save your QGIS work, disable pypopRF and close all instances using the affected profile. Check the exact installer error and ensure the ZIP was successfully built and verified. Other QGIS instances, antivirus or backup software can also retain a file handle; do not assume every lock comes from this plugin. Retry the valid ZIP with the plugin disabled. If an incomplete archive replaced files, reinstall the previous valid ZIP with the plugin disabled. The QGIS installer is not a transactional plugin backup.

If this does not recover the plugin, report the QGIS/OS versions and installer error without private data. Do not delete your project, engine cache or a broad QGIS profile as a repair step. A surviving engine job is not a reason to kill every Python process; cancellation and cleanup are scoped to the owned job.

docs.title: Input checks
docs.text:
All rasters must define a CRS, contain one band, and use the same pixel grid. Matching CRS and pixel size alone do not establish alignment: origin, rotation, extent and dimensions also matter. Prepare aligned rasters explicitly before analysis; use nearest-neighbour resampling for zone IDs and binary masks.

Census IDs must be unique finite integers matching zone IDs in the mastergrid. Population values must be finite and nonnegative. Repeated CSV column names are rejected. Custom ID and population column names are supported; validation does not rename columns in your original CSV.

Water masks use 1 for excluded water and 0 for land. Constraints use 1 for allowed support and 0 for excluded cells. Unknown mask coverage is excluded. A zone with positive population needs at least one eligible cell with a positive predicted weight; otherwise the run fails with the affected zone IDs. A single valid cell is supported. Zero-population zones receive zero within their eligible support.

Covariate NoData means unknown, unless the source dataset explicitly defines a different meaning. It is not automatically replaced by zero. Selected predictor rasters must provide usable values on cells where population is allocated.

New TIFF imports with external .msk, .aux.xml or world files are rejected because copying only the TIFF would change its interpretation. Create a self-contained aligned GeoTIFF with an internal validity mask before importing. Existing canonical project TIFFs retain their sidecars; these dataset resources are fingerprinted as inputs by the engine.

docs.title: Older model files
docs.text: Old separate model.pkl.gz / scaler.pkl.gz files do not record a complete prediction contract. Retrain the model to create model_bundle.pkl.gz. The bundle records its target transformation, ordered feature schema, runtime versions and grid geometry. Load only trusted local model files.

docs.title: A failed or cancelled analysis
docs.text: Read the terminal message and the run log. Do not interpret intermediate TIFFs in a failed run as completed population maps. Only a run with a complete manifest has passed the population checks. Cancel requests are cooperative; the current operation may need to finish before resources can be closed safely.

docs.title: Interpreting model quality
docs.text: Preserving census totals is a calculation invariant. It does not prove that the population is placed in the correct buildings or pixels. Validation metrics describe held-out census zones in population-per-supported-pixel units. Grouped or spatial validation must be interpreted according to its recorded split strategy; random-zone diagnostics do not establish spatial independence.

docs.title: What to include in a useful report
docs.text:
1. Plugin build, QGIS version, operating system and whether this is installation, engine setup, project opening, importing or running.
  2. Exact message from Details → Copy diagnostics, not only the final percent.
  3. For a run, its manifest.json and run log; for opening, a redacted configuration and the distinction between selected and active paths.
  4. Minimal reproduction with synthetic/public data when possible.

Redact personal paths, credentials, identifying census records and restricted source data. A screenshot may show filenames or user names; check it before posting to a public issue. Do not publish a whole project/cache/profile to obtain help.

docs.title: Development diagnostics
docs.text: Run python -m pytest in the development engine environment. Native QGIS tests require genuine QGIS/Qt bindings and are marked qgis. See the development guide for the maintained regression suites, package checks and native-test commands.
